The Argand diagram above shows the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $1.$
examples.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${\color{black}x_1= 2}$ and ${\color{black}x_{2,3}=-2\pm \textrm{i}}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is ${\color{black}a=1}.$ 

Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =(x-2)(x-(-2+\text{i}))(x-(-2-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)(x-(-2+\text{i}))(x-(-2-\text{i})) & = \\ (x-2)({x}^{2}-x(-2-\text{i})-x(-2+\text{i})+(-2+\text{i})(-2-\text{i})) & = \\ (x-2)({x}^{2}+4x+5) & = \\ {x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+5x-2{x}^{2}-8x-10 & = \\ {x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-3x-10 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x) = x^3+2x^2-3x-10.$

feedback.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $P(x).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=-4,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-1(x-(-5))(x-(-4))(x-(-3)) \\  & =-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+5)(x+4)(x+3) & =-({x}^{2}+9x+20)(x+3) \\  & =-({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+9{x}^{2}+27x+20x+60) \\  & =-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-47x-60.$
